title: Signed acceptance record (TRM-6)
$comment: The TRM-6 acceptance record (NOT an ATA authority record — ATA-6 requires both and keeps them distinct). Rail-neutral: `scheme` is a namespaced OPEN set (`<family>:<method>` — the family names the port answerable for it), `signer` is the scheme's canonical identifier, and `payloadType` is open for the same reason. The EVM family's registered forms are enforced conditionally below (a 0x-address signer under evm:*); other families validate at their port, which refuses (fail-closed) anything it does not implement. Seeded here because the vectors-first rule admits no exception for the artifact carrying the buyer's legal assent.

signer.description: the accepting party's identifier in the scheme's canonical form: a 0x-address for evm:* (enforced below), a key identifier (JWK thumbprint URI / kid) for a JOSE family, a base58 public key for an ed25519 rail, a DID where a family defines one

scheme.description: namespaced `<family>:<method>` — registered: evm:eip191, evm:eip712, evm:erc1271, evm:erc6492 (binding-evm-common). Open set: a new rail adds schemes with its port; an un-namespaced scheme names no family and is rejected

signedAt.description: RFC 3339 — TRM-6's required timestamp, the signer-attested claim; the settlement's chain-anchored time remains the independent anchor that corroborates or impeaches it (PRS-4/WLD-4)

payloadType.description: what the signature covers — registered: atrHash (the raw 32-byte fingerprint, rail-neutral), eip712-acceptance-envelope (the EVM typed-data envelope). Open set; a port refuses payload types it cannot reconstruct

grantRef.description: an lcp:sha256: reference to the ATA grant

allOf.$comment: the EVM family's canonical signer form — strict where the semantics are known, open where they are not
